Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ: INTU) reported an earnings beat for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, delivering broad-based double-digit revenue growth, expanding margins, and continued acceleration across its key platform businesses, including Credit Karma, QuickBooks Online, and Mailchimp. Despite these strong metrics, the stock closed down 2.03 percent on November 20, 2025, at 637.44 United States dollars. However, shares rebounded in after-hours trading by over 3 percent, recovering to 658.00 United States dollars, as investors absorbed management’s reaffirmation of full-year guidance.

The initial stock dip appeared to reflect short-term profit-taking after a strong pre-earnings run, rather than any fundamental weakness. With a forward price-to-earnings ratio of more than 46, valuation sensitivity likely played a role in the day’s volatility. Analysts covering the stock emphasized that institutional confidence remains intact, especially in light of CEO Sasan Goodarzi’s reaffirmation of Intuit’s platform vision centered on AI-driven financial services.

Yes, Intuit stock had a great Q1. But doesn't stock cost too much?

**Intuit **(INTU +3.02%) stock jumped 4.4% through Friday, 11:25 a.m. ET, after beating forecasts for fiscal Q1 2026 earnings last night.

Heading into the report, analysts predicted Intuit would earn $3.09 on under $3.8 billion in sales. In fact, Intuit earned $3.34 per share, and sales approached $3.9 billion.

Image source: Getty Images.

## Intuit Q1 earnings

CEO Sasan Goodarzi hailed \"an exceptional first quarter.\" He said Intuit is continuing \"to execute on our AI-driven expert platform strategy.\" (Yes, you read that right. Intuit is now an AI stock).

Sales grew 18%, and profits improved even further. Operating income nearly doubled (up 97%), and net earnings, as calculated according to generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), *more *than doubled, up 127%.

Those GAAP earnings weren't as good as the \"$3.34\" earned pro forma, but Intuit's $1.59 per share in GAAP profit was more than enough to give the stock a big lift this morning.

Guidance was also great. Near-term, management forecasts revenue growth of 14% to 15% in fiscal Q2, along with GAAP earnings of between $1.76 and $1.81 per share.

Intuit says by the end of fiscal 2026 it should have racked up revenue of more than $21 billion -- maybe as much as $21.2 billion -- for 12% to 13% growth. Operating profit should grow about 18%, and GAAP net profit will rise 13% to 15% -- $15.49 to $15.69 per share.
